scope: Editorial shortlist from the saved positive KR-110/120/140 cases and LK-202 chapter packages. Not an exhaustive review of millions of unreviewed records; not publication approval.

candidates.title: A source guide through all six chapters of Ephesians
candidates.finding: The saved packages connect Ephesians to actual exposition sections, with 145 Fergusson samples tied to held reader locations and 35 Calvin samples retained privately.
candidates.benefit: A reader can move from the chapter they are studying to a relevant commentary section instead of searching whole books.
candidates.placement: Bible reader → Ephesians → Sources on this passage
candidates.format: A short source description, why it belongs here, and a reliable reading destination.
candidates.next: Review the prose and source identity for the complete six-chapter guide; resolve the Ephesians 1:6 conflict and verify current reader destinations before integration.
candidates.scale: One reusable passage-to-source component could serve more books after each book passes the same review. The current evidence supports Ephesians only.
candidates.novelty: Prepared connections; visitor-facing integration remains unfinished.
candidates.limits: 180 location samples are not 180 approved explanations. Forty Fergusson transcription gaps remain recorded. Calvin's exact edition lacks a verified on-site reading copy. Output-specific source-use review is pending.

candidates.title: Ephesians 4: unity and a church growing to maturity
candidates.finding: Waldron explains the ministry gifts in Ephesians 4 as serving the church's maturity. Bavinck describes unity as already present while still being worked out in the church's life.
candidates.benefit: Give the reader two substantive treatments of the same passage, with a clear reason to open each.
candidates.format: Two attributed reading cards; no claim that these authors represent every Christian tradition.
candidates.next: Check the complete arguments, exact edition/translator credits and a usable source destination; write one accurate sentence introducing each.
candidates.scale: The useful unit is a passage with a few well-chosen sources. More sources count only when they add a distinct explanation.
candidates.novelty: Candidate reading connections from held works.
candidates.limits: This is a draft description of these source positions, not a doctrinal ruling. Bavinck's held English edition needs its edition and translation credits checked.

candidates.title: The Lord's Supper: Hodge's questions beside the source passages
candidates.finding: A. A. Hodge's Outlines of Theology names the institution passages and explains the terms Lord's Supper, cup of blessing, table and communion. Matthew Henry explains the name used in 1 Corinthians 11:20.
candidates.benefit: A reader gets a clear route from the biblical passage to a structured theological discussion.
candidates.placement: Bible reader → 1 Corinthians 11; Teachers → A. A. Hodge → Outlines of Theology
candidates.format: An attributed study-source card with the held text available to inspect.
candidates.next: Use the readable held EPUB witness for this item, verify the reader against it, and preserve the work/edition distinction from the separate PDF and TXT.
candidates.scale: Structured question-and-answer works can supply useful reading guides after their text and headings are checked.
candidates.novelty: A specific usable passage in the held Hodge text, not proof that every Hodge representation is sound.
candidates.limits: These are Protestant source explanations. They must not become an unlabelled Catholic sacramental answer or a claim that all editions have been OCR-verified.

candidates.title: A reading path for bereavement and hope
candidates.finding: J. R. Miller addresses the question of how to continue after a bereavement. Spurgeon's October 2 morning reading connects future hope with present endurance and activity.
candidates.benefit: Offer a small, purposeful reading path with a reason for each selection, rather than a pile of results containing the word sorrow.
candidates.format: A short editorial introduction followed by two attributed devotional readings.
candidates.next: Review the complete pastoral context and tone, select self-contained passages, and check the exact editions and source-use conditions.
candidates.scale: Repeat for a limited set of real reader concerns only after each reading path has been reviewed.
candidates.novelty: A possible curated reading path; the underlying writings already exist.
candidates.limits: Historical devotional counsel is not a clinical intervention. The introduction must not impose a single explanation of another person's loss.

candidates.title: When prayer feels dry: historical pastoral readings
candidates.finding: Rous discusses spiritual consolation; Whitefield explicitly introduces deadness and dryness in prayer as a pastoral concern.
candidates.benefit: Help someone locate older pastoral writing on the experience they are asking about, even when its vocabulary differs from modern search terms.
candidates.format: A labelled historical reading guide with intact surrounding context.
candidates.next: Extend the Whitefield selection past its introduction before summarising his counsel; select a complete readable passage and retain the recorded editorial gap.
candidates.scale: Potentially useful for narrowly defined reading concerns. The saved retrieval gain was one question, not proof of general search reliability.
candidates.novelty: One of the saved retrieval improvements, requiring editorial completion.
candidates.limits: The selected Whitefield window starts a discussion and breaks before the whole argument. It should not be presented as a complete answer.

candidates.title: Forgiveness after injury: read the actual pastoral arguments
candidates.finding: Tillotson appeals to the example of Christ and to our own need of forgiveness. Winslow's devotional work offers another treatment of forgiving injuries.
candidates.benefit: Present a focused pair of readings on a concrete concern, with the source's argument available for inspection.
candidates.format: Attributed reading recommendations, with qualifications preserved.
candidates.next: Review the complete sections before stating distinctions about friendship, trust or reconciliation; the visible Tillotson window alone does not establish all of them.
candidates.scale: A useful pattern for practical reading collections, provided each source contributes a distinct, complete treatment.
candidates.novelty: A curated selection rather than a new theological finding.
candidates.limits: Do not imply that forgiveness requires unsafe contact. Overlapping Winslow windows are one source contribution, not several independent witnesses.

candidates.title: Brooks and Goodwin on temptation and preserving faith
candidates.finding: The selected Brooks passage treats having God as one's portion as a defence against temptation. Goodwin discusses the divine power needed to sustain faith.
candidates.benefit: Give an author-comparison page something concrete to compare, with two actual source passages rather than topic badges.
candidates.format: Two attributed passages and a carefully limited comparison.
candidates.next: Verify complete local speaker roles and avoid the Burroughs works whose composite metadata also names Goodwin.
candidates.scale: Author comparisons become useful when the same narrow question is answered by identified passages from distinct works.
candidates.novelty: A candidate comparison; no new consensus or influence claim.
candidates.limits: The original retrieval mixed contributor roles and repeated Brooks representations. Those mistakes must not be carried into the website.

candidates.title: Gill and Boyce: what does faith do in justification?
candidates.finding: Boyce distinguishes faith as an instrument from the cause or ground of justification. Gill treats Christ's righteousness and its imputation in his account of justification.
candidates.benefit: Let a reader compare a precise theological distinction in two identified authors' own discussions.
candidates.format: A narrow comparison with source excerpts, objections and replies kept separate.
candidates.next: Review the complete sections, resolve duplicate representations and write an attributed comparison that does not turn a quoted objection into an author's own view.
candidates.scale: This can support a coherent library of focused comparisons; it does not validate an automatic doctrine-comparison engine.
candidates.novelty: A source-backed comparison candidate, not an extracted settled answer.
candidates.limits: Both are Protestant sources. The page must label that scope and preserve specific Catholic doctrinal cautions where applicable.

candidates.title: Bunyan and Flavel on perseverance
candidates.finding: The saved passages pair Flavel's definition and grounds of perseverance with Bunyan's account of dependence on God's preserving power.
candidates.benefit: Replace a vague shared-topic link with a readable comparison of two actual arguments.
candidates.format: Two distinct works with an attributed summary and source context.
candidates.next: Check the full arguments and exact editions; exclude Mason/editorial notes in Pilgrim's Progress from Bunyan's own testimony.
candidates.scale: One question, two identifiable authors, a small number of distinct works.
candidates.novelty: A candidate comparison from held texts.
candidates.limits: Duplicate Flavel representations do not count as independent sources. This is not a cross-tradition conclusion.

candidates.title: Hebrews 8: compare two readings of the new covenant
candidates.finding: Pink applies the quoted new-covenant promise to Christians. Gunn disputes a dispensational reading of the Hebrews/Jeremiah connection.
candidates.benefit: Show how identified writers use the passage, including the interpretive disagreement being addressed.
candidates.format: Labelled source positions with a concise explanation of the question being disputed.
candidates.next: Review the complete arguments and source-use conditions; identify the target position accurately before writing the comparison.
candidates.scale: Supports passage-specific interpretation guides when viewpoints and coverage gaps are explicit.
candidates.novelty: A possible interpretation guide using existing writings.
candidates.limits: Two selected sources are not a balanced survey of Christianity. Their conclusions are source positions, not site-wide doctrinal endorsement.

candidates.title: Hebrews 6: locate the full argument about apostasy
candidates.finding: The retained Pink and Owen passages address the warning and the relation of outward instruction, inward grace and apostasy.
candidates.benefit: Give the reader identified discussions of the difficult passage instead of incidental references to it.
candidates.format: Two source cards with their interpretive scope stated.
candidates.next: Review the complete sections and distinguish reported objections from the author's replies. Do not reuse the wrong-chapter Owen result.
candidates.scale: A repeatable difficult-passage reading aid, subject to source and editorial review.
candidates.novelty: Located reading candidates.
candidates.limits: This is a narrow selection of theological positions, with no independent doctrinal review.

candidates.title: Psalm 51: Hildersham on public repentance
candidates.finding: Hildersham's lectures discuss David's public repentance and the publication of his confession in the setting of Psalm 51.
candidates.benefit: Point to a sustained historical treatment of repentance rather than a source that merely cites the psalm.
candidates.format: A brief attributed introduction and a usable location in the held work.
candidates.next: Check readability, full context and the reader destination before selecting the passage.
candidates.scale: Especially useful for older lecture/commentary collections when their sections are navigable.
candidates.novelty: A reading recommendation from an existing work.
candidates.limits: The stored excerpt and source spelling are not a complete modern edition or a newly verified interpretation of the psalm.

candidates.title: Follow Piper's named Whitefield quotation back to the sermon
candidates.finding: Piper explicitly introduces Whitefield's argument about election and humility. A matching passage is located in the held Whitefield sermon.
candidates.benefit: Let a reader inspect the source behind a quotation and see its surrounding argument.
candidates.placement: Teachers → Source trails / Scholars → documented textual connections
candidates.format: A named quotation trail with both witnesses and clear edition identities.
candidates.next: Verify the complete quotation and its boundaries, check the exact editions and proposed excerpt use, and confirm that this trail is not already represented.
candidates.scale: Strong named quotations can support a useful source-tracing feature. Generic wording similarity cannot replace this evidence.
candidates.novelty: A specific documented quotation connection, pending comparison with existing source trails.
candidates.limits: This supports this quotation only. It does not establish general influence, agreement, or that millions of wording pairs are publishable.

candidates.title: Judging motives: Godolphin alongside Pink
candidates.finding: Both passages use Matthew 7:1 and Romans 14:4 to discuss unjust judgment and intruding on God's prerogative. Pink explicitly distinguishes suspicion from established facts.
candidates.benefit: A useful comparative reading on a concrete ethical question, with the connection explained.
candidates.format: Two source readings and a short explanation of the shared question.
candidates.next: Read the complete passages, verify local attribution in Godolphin's compilation, and retain differences in scope.
candidates.scale: Reference matches can feed carefully reviewed comparisons; only the selected comparison is recommended here.
candidates.novelty: A possible substantive cross-work reading connection.
candidates.limits: Shared references establish neither agreement in every detail nor literary dependence.

candidates.title: God's word and its effects: Haldane alongside Sikes
candidates.finding: The two contexts connect Isaiah 55:11 and 2 Corinthians 2:16 with God's word accomplishing effects of life or death, within different larger arguments.
candidates.benefit: Show why two passages are worth reading together, beyond saying that they share Bible references.
candidates.placement: Study → Scripture and preaching → Related readings
candidates.format: An attributed comparison with both larger arguments acknowledged.
candidates.next: Review the complete arguments and readability; avoid presenting Sikes's unusual surrounding claims as a generic Christian consensus.
candidates.scale: A candidate for selective thematic reading, not an automatic related-passages feed.
candidates.novelty: A candidate cross-work connection.
candidates.limits: The connection is narrower than either author's full doctrine. Similar references do not prove influence.

candidates.title: Knowing God: Purnell and Warner on two contrasting texts
candidates.finding: Both passages contrast knowing God in John 17:3 with the judgment text in 2 Thessalonians 1:8.
candidates.benefit: Offer an explained pair of historical readings on a precise question.
candidates.format: Two credited readings with readable source excerpts.
candidates.next: Review the full contexts and source quality, verify identities and destinations, and decide whether this adds enough beyond the stronger comparisons.
candidates.scale: Useful only if the comparison contributes something distinct to an existing study path.
candidates.novelty: A candidate comparison, with lower immediate priority.
candidates.limits: The saved match is not a complete theological synthesis or evidence of literary borrowing.

candidates.title: Let readers inspect the 1644 confession's own preface
candidates.finding: The held text prints a 1644 imprint and explains that the churches are responding to accusations made against them.
candidates.benefit: Ground a short historical introduction in the document's own stated purpose rather than a loose date or an unsourced biography.
candidates.format: A document context card distinguishing imprint, preface and later interpretation.
candidates.next: Verify the transcription against the held edition, check signatory/edition identities and compare against material already on the site.
candidates.scale: A useful pattern for document introductions; it does not create verified event chronology automatically.
candidates.novelty: A source-backed context candidate.
candidates.limits: A printed date and an author's account of purpose are evidence about the document, not independent verification of all surrounding historical claims.

candidates.title: Boyce's work in theological education, from his title and dedication
candidates.finding: The held title names Boyce's professorship at Southern Baptist Theological Seminary; the dedication discusses an endowed theology chair and ministerial education.
candidates.benefit: Give an author/work page a sourced account of the book's educational setting.
candidates.placement: Teachers → James P. Boyce → Abstract of Systematic Theology
candidates.format: A concise source-backed work introduction, retaining transcriber and edition credits.
candidates.next: Compare with the existing profile; add only a missing useful fact, verify the exact edition and keep publication date separate from author life events.
candidates.scale: A reliable author/work layer helps users choose what to read. It is supporting infrastructure rather than a new research discovery.
candidates.novelty: Potential profile enrichment; current-site duplication must be checked.
candidates.limits: The title/dedication does not independently prove every biographical claim about Boyce.

candidates.title: Caritas, charity and love in one identified commentary witness
candidates.finding: The saved Calvin commentary window contains numbered Latin and English blocks for 1 Corinthians 13:4–8, followed by English exposition.
candidates.benefit: Show a real local language correspondence with its edition context, rather than claim that two similar words settle a translation question.
candidates.format: A small bilingual source note, with translator identity and numbering checked.
candidates.next: Identify the English edition/translator and verify the full local correspondence before publication.
candidates.scale: Useful as selected language notes. This one witness supplies no global translation alignment.
candidates.novelty: A local correspondence in a held edition.
candidates.limits: English wording is not Calvin's original English composition; translator identity remains unresolved in this saved retrieval.

candidates.title: Show where an editor speaks instead of the original author
candidates.finding: The held Calvin Notes window distinguishes Latin source wording, an English rendering and explanation explicitly marked Ed., including a textual-reading uncertainty.
candidates.benefit: Prevent a reader or an author-comparison feature from assigning editorial explanation to Calvin.
candidates.format: A labelled source note separating author, translator and editor.
candidates.next: Verify the edition and editor identity, preserve the conjectural reading and select the complete note.
candidates.scale: Correct voice attribution improves every downstream comparison. This is a quality correction with broad reuse, not a new doctrinal finding.
candidates.novelty: A useful source-role distinction.
candidates.limits: A signed Ed. label distinguishes the role but does not by itself identify the editor.

candidates.title: A small Hebrew/Aramaic dictionary lookup
candidates.finding: The held entries connect Hebrew אָב and Aramaic אַב with source-authored English glosses for father, while retaining the language distinction.
candidates.benefit: Let a reader consult an identified dictionary entry without leaving the study context.
candidates.format: The term, language, entry identity and recorded gloss; no automatic verse translation.
candidates.next: Review the lexicon's entry identifiers, credits and proposed use; connect only to the correct word/entry and context.
candidates.scale: 17,977 lexicon links can support dictionary browsing after entry mapping and review. The much larger ORACC token-gloss collection is a different resource.
candidates.novelty: A lookup over existing dictionary content, not a newly discovered meaning.
candidates.limits: A dictionary gloss does not select the right sense in a biblical passage. Hebrew and Aramaic entries are not interchangeable.
